gen-fs-red-hat-display-gf-solway: Solway keeps its strokes flat and stencil-like. Beside Red Hat Display's marker-line headings, its bookish serif voice would carry a long page with quiet authority and plenty of daylight in every curve.
gen-fs-red-hat-display-gf-spectral-sc: Spectral SC is literary and bookish, with sturdy hairlines and wide mouths on its round forms. Spectral SC gives Red Hat Display's smooth, tube-like headings a thoughtful partner, bold up top and finely shaded below.
gen-fs-red-hat-display-gf-stix-two-text: Editorial in temperament, Red Hat Display draws every line like a smooth tube with daylight inside each curve. STIX Two Text follows with mild, visible contrast and pulled-back terminals, so a long read feels traditional and unhurried.
gen-fs-red-hat-display-gf-tai-heritage-p: Marker-smooth and modern, Red Hat Display shows no thick-and-thin shifts at all. Tai Heritage Pro is the dignified foil, a text serif whose strokes carry a modest weight change and a clear channel into each round letter.
gen-fs-red-hat-display-gf-taviraj: Bookish by nature, Taviraj sits between monoline and sharp contrast. Under Red Hat Display's ballpoint-pen headings, its generous curve gaps would let a long page unroll with an editorial, easy rhythm.
gen-fs-red-hat-display-gf-trirong: Red Hat Display's lines have the texture of neatly bent pipe cleaner, bold and contemporary with light inside every curve. And Trirong, a dignified serif with softly varied strokes and gently flared ends, reads smoothly across a long stretch.
gen-fs-red-hat-display-gf-trocchi: Trocchi has a wide-open ring of a c and bowls that thin gracefully, like brushed watercolor. Trocchi's quiet weight shift gives Red Hat Display's unmodulated, marker-like headings a dignified, classic counterpart, and that is the strongest thing here.
gen-fs-red-hat-display-gf-trykker: Red Hat Display's bowls never thin at the sides. Trykker, a refined text serif, adds understated thick-thin contrast that neither jolts nor flattens, and that tempered shift is where this pairing is strongest.
gen-fs-red-hat-display-gf-uchen: Uchen reads dignified and refined, its lowercase curves welcoming the eye inside. Uchen holds a long stretch with restraint, its thinnest strokes still sturdy, while Red Hat Display's brush-free lines stay flat and modern.
gen-fs-red-hat-display-gf-vollkorn-sc: Red Hat Display draws its bowls at stem thickness, bold and modern. Vollkorn SC brings sturdy hairlines and loosely spaced, literary letters, so the two feel like a poster beside a well-worn book.
